stemBlocks.value: The diagram shows quadrilateral PQRS with vertices P(-3, 0), Q(0, 4), R(3, 0) and S(0, -4). (a) Calculate the length of each side.
Think first: Read the four vertices off the grid, then it is four applications of the same distance formula.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p129-q08 from workbook page 129.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the vertices from the grid.

contentBlocks.value: The marked points are P(-3, 0), Q(0, 4), R(3, 0), S(0, -4)

strategyBlocks.value: Read P, Q, R and S from the graph and apply d = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²) to the four sides PQ, QR, RS and SP.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) PQ = QR = RS = SP = 5 units — all four sides are 5 units long.

whyThisWorks.value: Each side spans 3 units horizontally and 4 units vertically, so each is the hypotenuse of the same 3–4–5 right-angled triangle. Because squaring kills the signs, the direction of travel around the quadrilateral does not change any length. Four equal sides is the defining property of a rhombus, which is what the symmetry of the diagram suggests.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading a vertex as (4, 0) instead of (0, 4) — swapping the x- and y-coordinates.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading a vertex as (4, 0) instead of (0, 4) — swapping the x- and y-coordinates.
